subject: Urgent: token throughput drop & p99 spike after quant rollout (RapidRetail)
messages:
From: Maria Ortega <maria.ortega@rapidretail.com>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, support@rapidretail.com
Date: Tue, 3 Oct 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spike + token/s drop since Sep 29 rollout

Hi Evelyn / Redwood team,

We started seeing elevated p95/p99 latency and a roughly 40% drop in token-per-second throughput on our hosted endpoints starting late Friday (Sep 29) after you rolled the quantization profile. Attached are a few samples and traces from our side. Error rates are still low but tail latency makes our user-facing autocomplete feature unusable during traffic bursts.

Key observations from our Ops: 
- p95 increased from ~120ms to ~420ms, p99 from ~210ms to ~1.2s on average.
- Token/sec (per-request steady-state) dropped from ~380 to ~220 on identical prompt set.
- The change correlates with model variant: redwood/gptx-16q (quantized) — previous non-quant variant did not show this.

We need an update within 2 business hours. This is impacting peak traffic for our mobile users.

Attached: throughput-sample-20281003.csv, p99-traces-20281003.zip

Thanks,
Maria Ortega
Head of Platform Reliability
RapidRetail

Date: Tue, 3 Oct 2028 16:49:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 spike + token/s drop since Sep 29 rollout

Evelyn — thanks for the ping. Initial triage notes: 
- We reproduced the token/s drop on a small test harness using the RedBench prompt set with redwood/gptx-16q and the new kernel-selection table that shipped 09-29.
- Profiling shows increased per-token kernel-switch overhead around longer context windows (>= 512). It looks like the new kernel routing is selecting a slower kernel path for some attention head shapes when sequence length increases.
- KV cache hit behavior appears unchanged; no obvious lock contention.

Immediate mitigation plan I can run now:
1) Roll the kernel-selection map for the gptx-16q variant back to the previous mapping (fast path) for customers in "enterprise-tier" routing (RapidRetail).
2) If rolling map does not restore TPS within 30min, revert to the non-quantized model shard for their route as a hotfix.

I'll try option 1 first and report back in 20–30 minutes.

-- Vivek
Engineering, Runtime & Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Oct 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 spike + token/s drop since Sep 29 rollout

Good reproduction — I dug into the rollout notes (rollout-notes-20280929.pdf) and the kernel selector delta. Two things to call out: 
- The new mapping added a cost heuristic that prefers int8-friendly kernels for certain layer dim splits. That's optimal for latency on medium sequences (<256) but can regress on long sequences due to increased micro-batch fragmentation.
- We also changed a quant packing routine that slightly alters memory alignment; on some Ampere variants that interacts with kernel prefetch and raises instruction-level latency.

Action I'm taking:
- Approving Vivek's rollback of the selector map for enterprise routes now.
- Preparing a safe fallback play: automated route-level model bump to the floating-point variant (gptx-16) if rollback doesn't restore baseline.

I'll run the rollback and post telemetry in 25m.

-Markus
Principal Architect, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Oct 2028 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p99 spike + token/s drop since Sep 29 rollout

Rollout update: I rolled back the kernel-selection map for the gptx-16q variant on RapidRetail's route at 17:12 PDT. Preliminary metrics: 
- Token/sec recovered from ~220 -> ~360 on our simulated user trace for 90th percentile sessions.
- p95 dropped from ~420ms -> ~150ms; p99 improved from ~1.2s -> ~260ms in the sampled window.
- No errors introduced; autoscaling held steady.

Next steps: keep rollback for 4 hours and observe production metrics. Markus will run a targeted regression test matrix to reproduce the micro-batch fragmentation effect across hardware families. We should follow up with a postmortem and a more conservative kernel-cost heuristic.

I will ask RapidRetail if they want a temporary route model bump to gptx-16 (non-quant) as an added safety, but metrics look promising after the selector rollback.

-- Vivek

We can also schedule a brief call to review next steps (conservative rollout gating + optional temporary model bump). Are you available at 10am PT on Thursday?
